clue.text: Game not to be played with electrical equipment

indicators.note: letters to be played with are toyed about and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that some game is not meant to be played near electrical gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be played with' rearranges GAME plus NOT; 'Game not to be played' reads like a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A small generator with permanent magnets, used for ignition in engines, is an electrical device.

clue.text: Urge cheat to make a real effort

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat them
to strain is to try very hard

explanation.surface: Advice that pushing a cheat into trying properly takes some doing.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge or compel someone is to force them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Standing allows little latitude

explanation.surface: Someone's status leaves them hardly any freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little latitude' looks like freedom of action, but it means one small unit of geographical latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing means rank or level in society; a small unit on the globe's grid of latitude is one of 360 parts of a circle.

clue.text: Put into words by crack journalist

parts.note: a report is the bang of a gun, a crack
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Something was written up by an expert reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' reads as an adjective meaning skilled, but it is the noise of a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stated or related something in speech or writing is a synonym.

clue.text: The writer of the novel "Cherry and Almond"

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about who wrote a book titled Cherry and Almond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book itself; it signals rearranging CHERRY AND ALMOND into the author of The Big Sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The American crime novelist who created Philip Marlowe is an example of an author.

clue.text: A woman's resignation

explanation.surface: A lady has given notice and quit her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resignation' suggests leaving a job; here it means calm acceptance, and the woman is a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's given name, and also the quality of calmly enduring trouble without complaint.

clue.text: Jolly fellow, a high-flier no longer

definitions.text: Jolly fellow, a high-flier no longer

parts.words: Jolly fellow, a high-flier no longer
parts.note: the Jolly flag of skull and crossbones was once hoisted high by pirates, who no longer fly it

explanation.surface: A cheerful chap who has fallen from his former success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly fellow' sounds like a cheerful man; it completes the name of the pirate flag, which once flew at the masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name that also completes the name of the pirate flag, a banner flown aloft in past centuries.

clue.text: Issue Number I with current back-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, back-up says the whole string is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: A publication note about Number I and a current backup copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' reads as a spare copy; it turns NO, I and TIDE upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a magazine or newspaper is one printing of it.

clue.text: Promise the page a part

parts.note: an actor's role is their part

explanation.surface: A director pledges the page boy a part in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner's word of honour, given on early release, is a pledge.

clue.text: Still, a profit can be made repeatedly

parts.note: still in the sense of nevertheless gives yet
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Advice that, even so, money can be made over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb of time but means nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Once more, over and over again: an idiom for something happening a further time.

clue.text: A scientist rang most excitedly

indicators.note: doing something excitedly throws it about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A researcher made a phone call in a state of great excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges RANG MOST; Anders Ångström was a Swedish physicist who studied spectra.
explanation.definitionFit: A nineteenth-century Swedish physicist, after whom a tiny unit of length is named.

clue.text: Six-footer from a village near Wigan

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words near Wigan

explanation.surface: A tall person who comes from a village close to Wigan, a town in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it means a creature with six legs, an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect, with six legs like all insects, known for its pincers.

clue.text: A way to encourage the serving of fish

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A method of persuading diners to eat the fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving of fish' reads as a dish, but 'fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fish whose eggs are eaten as caviar.

clue.text: Preparing deed — can't appear corrupt

indicators.note: preparing the words means working them into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drawing up a document that must not look dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally degenerate or self-indulgent, a synonym for debased.

clue.text: Pessimistic newspaper men going into action

indicators.note: going into says the reporters are placed inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: Gloomy reporters getting involved in some activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low and gloomy about things, close to downbeat.

clue.text: Playing, but not playing fair

explanation.surface: Someone is taking part in a game, but cheating at it.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is playing the violin, the other cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a violin, and also cheating or swindling.

clue.text: High-fibre food one has to shake

parts.note: bran is the high-fibre part of cereal
a dish is a portion of food

explanation.surface: Someone has a bowl of high-fibre cereal and shakes it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shake' looks like a milkshake to go with the cereal; it means wave about.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave something threateningly, as one waves a sword.

clue.text: Wild behaviour of a politician in anger

indicators.note: in places a politician inside the word for anger

parts.note: rage is anger
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician's furious outburst described as wild behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent, uncontrolled spree is wild conduct.

clue.text: A feature of the church-up to a point

definitions.text: A feature of the church-up to a point

parts.words: A feature of the church-up to a point
parts.note: a part of a church building that rises upwards and ends in a sharp tip

explanation.surface: Something is only partly true of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to a point' reads as partly; it means rising to a sharp tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall tower with a spire on a church building rises to a tip.

clue.text: Sound bill set before a junior minister

indicators.note: set before puts the bill ahead of the minister in the answer

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a curate is an assistant clergyman, a junior minister of the church

explanation.surface: An honest invoice is presented before a junior government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junior minister' suggests government; it means a curate in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and exact, as in a sound argument.

clue.text: The firm's doctors cover the entire world

parts.note: CO is company, a firm, with possessive S
MOs are medical officers, doctors

explanation.surface: A company's doctors provide cover across the whole globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' looks like insurance; it is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe seen as an ordered whole.

clue.text: Gladdened to find a large number in employment

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
used means employed, put to work

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased to see many people in jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertained and made to smile, as when pleased.

clue.text: The back that's rigid

explanation.surface: A person's spine is stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the rear of a ship, the other strict.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear of a boat, and severe or strict.

clue.text: Underworld bloomer resulting in bad accident

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
an aster is a flower, a bloomer

explanation.surface: A criminal's blunder ends in a nasty crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake; here it means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a serious mishap.

clue.text: Data of some concern

explanation.surface: Information that matters.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is raw information, the other relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Information collected for a book, and relevant or significant.

clue.text: Exercises inside but in full view

indicators.note: inside places the exercises within the word for but

parts.note: only means but, merely
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Workouts done indoors yet visible to all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like indoors; it signals one piece placed inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Done publicly with nothing hidden.

clue.text: The youngster, being green, ate out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inexperienced young person goes out for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' reads as inexperienced; here it is anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: A person aged thirteen to nineteen is a young person.
